item.title: Connecticut man sentenced to two years for $3.5M Amazon trucking fraud
item.description:
Ameer Nasir, a 25‑year‑old from Trumbull, Connecticut, was sentenced on Wednesday to two years in federal prison for defrauding Amazon Logistics of more than $3.5 million. He had registered 23 trucking accounts with Amazon Relay, which prosecutors tied to over 1,000 nonexistent trailer moves.
The scheme ran from December 2019 through February 2021, during which Nasir used the accounts to obtain transportation assignments and falsely check trailers in and out via Amazon Relay. Prosecutors said he evaded Relay’s GPS geofencing safeguard by misusing the platform’s manual override, and one May 16, 2020, assignment from Kent, Washington, to Lakeland, Florida, was billed at $4,566.41 although the trailer never moved. Nasir pleaded guilty to one wire fraud count on March 6, 2026, and the court ordered $3,547,090.93 in restitution plus three years of supervised release.
Amazon has since added identity and driver verification measures to its Relay platform to curb fraud, according to earlier FreightWaves reporting. The scheme ended in February 2021, and the indictment shows Nasir exploited the system more than five years ago, leaving uncertain whether a similar fraud could succeed today.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/man-gets-2-years-for-3-5m-amazon-fraud-using-23-trucking-accounts)

item.title: Australian shoppers plan to spend $346 on Black Friday, up from $324 last year
item.description:
Australian shoppers intend to spend an average of $346 over the 2026 Black Friday Cyber Monday period, up from $324 last year, according to Shopify’s holiday retail report. This rise contrasts with a global decline in planned spending from $276 to $268, while 54% of respondents said economic conditions influenced their holiday purchases, prompting extra research before buying.
The report found that 85% of Australian shoppers prefer waiting to purchase a specific item rather than choosing an immediate alternative, compared with a global average of 79%. It also showed that 62% of Australian consumers expect to use AI tools for deal discovery and product comparison, with 70% of shoppers aged 25 to 34 already using such tools versus 45% across all age groups. Among businesses, 51% are investing in AI-generated content, 46% in virtual assistants and 45% in optimising store platforms for AI recommendation engines. The findings also highlight shifting merchant choices, with 54% of respondents reporting increased purchases from independent or niche brands compared to the previous year.
“Australians are still willing to spend this holiday season, but they’re putting more work into deciding what’s worth their money,” James Johnson, head of enterprise ANZ at Shopify said.
The findings come from Shopify’s holiday retail report. Australian consumers anticipate higher spending during the 2026 Black Friday Cyber Monday period even amid ongoing economic pressures.
Source: Internet Retailing Australia (https://internetretailing.com.au/australian-shoppers-set-to-increase-black-friday-spending)

item.title: Fast Retailing posts 32% profit rise to 743.1 billion yen
item.description:
Fast Retailing reported operating profit of 743.13 billion yen for the year ended August 31, a rise of about 32 percent from 564.3 billion yen a year earlier. The company forecast operating profit of 830 billion yen for the year ending August 2027, exceeding its own 730 billion yen target and the average analyst estimate of 726.45 billion yen.
Fast Retailing operates more than 2,500 Uniqlo stores worldwide, with nearly 900 of them in China, its largest foreign market. A weak yen raised import costs in Japan, pressuring fourth‑quarter results and prompting the company to consider price increases there. Fast Retailing plans to double the number of its flagship‑store format in Japan to 20 over the next decade to counter online competition and revive foot traffic.
The Uniqlo operator has beaten quarterly expectations throughout the year and repeatedly raised its profit guidance. Fast Retailing traces its origins to a single Uniqlo store opened in Hiroshima in 1984 and has since expanded to over 2,500 stores worldwide.
Source: Inside Retail Asia (https://insideretail.asia/2026/10/08/uniqlo-parent-fast-retailing-shocks-with-32-per-cent-profit-boost)

item.title: WEX executive says AI agents need payment controls to act safely
item.description:
At the PYMNTS B2B Payments Event 2026, Ryan Taylor, SVP Product Management – Mobility & Payments at WEX, said AI agents need three elements—context, controls, and clarity—to act safely. He noted that virtual cards already restrict merchant, amount, timing and transaction count, turning those limits into programmable permissions for machines.
Payment data supplies the context AI needs, showing who is spending, where money moves, what is bought and whether a transaction looks odd. While AI can decide that an invoice should be paid or a fuel purchase is legitimate, only the payment system can enforce whether the agent actually has authority to move the money. Taylor warned against giving agents open-ended access to corporate bank accounts, saying controls must govern how and when they can execute payments and how money flows to manage risk. He suggested the future enterprise payments stack could work less like traditional plumbing and more like an API that grants financial authority on demand.
“Taylor argued that effective artificial intelligence systems therefore require three elements: context, controls and clarity,” Ryan Taylor, SVP Product Management – Mobility & Payments at WEX said.
“One of the main reasons virtual cards are so compelling as we look towards an agentic future is that controls are built directly into the payments themselves,” Ryan Taylor, SVP Product Management – Mobility & Payments at WEX said.
Before this discussion, enterprises had to stitch together operational data and payment execution manually, a process that created delays and errors as transaction volumes grew. AI systems have improved at spotting suspicious invoices, fueling anomalies and price drifts, but they lacked the authority to act on those insights.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/b2b-payments/2026/b2b-payments-already-have-the-controls-ai-agents-need)

item.title: PYMNTS report splits U.S. consumers into three spending groups as prices rise
item.description:
PYMNTS Intelligence’s 2026 analysis finds that 45% of U.S. adults keep spending flat or raise it despite higher bills, while 34% cut both spending and savings and 21% boost income or rely on installment plans. Among the proactive group, 48% use buy now, pay later to manage expenses, compared with just 8% of the reactive group.
The report also notes that 66% of all consumers have reduced everyday spending and 51% have avoided large purchases, yet only 21% have tried negotiating bills. Side work is common, with 37.6% of workers having taken on extra jobs in the prior six months to supplement income. Within the baby‑boomer generation, 69% of reactive consumers report daily living pressure, a 31‑point gap versus the 38% of balanced boomers facing the same strain.
PYMNTS Intelligence’s “The Fragmented Paycheck: Why Rising Spending No Longer Means Stronger Demand,” part of The American Paycheck 2026 Annual Edition, examines how households earn, spend and manage financial pressure. It draws on four research programs covering financial lifestyles, generational behavior, credit use and consumer expectations.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/consumer-insights/2026/higher-prices-are-splitting-consumers-into-three-camps)

item.title: Amazon cuts about 1,000 roles in latest workforce reduction
item.description:
Amazon eliminated approximately 1,000 roles across its Stores, customer service, marketplace support and retail engineering teams on 6 October 2026. The cuts were disclosed via internal emails and affected employees in India and the UK, according to messages from an internal Slack channel with nearly 37,000 members. These reductions follow two earlier rounds that removed about 30,000 roles in October 2025 and January 2026.
An Amazon spokesperson told Business Insider that only a small number of positions, mainly in the Stores business, were eliminated that day. Employees asked about severance packages, medical leave, internal transfer options and whether further notifications would follow. Amazon has also reached out to former workers, including those from prior layoffs, to fill openings in its Amazon Web Services and artificial intelligence divisions.
“a small number,” Amazon spokesperson said.
Since late 2022, Amazon has eliminated more than 57,000 corporate positions. This includes the 16,000 roles cut in January 2026 and the roughly 30,000 roles removed in the two rounds announced in October 2025 and January 2026.
Source: Retail Insight Network (https://retail-insight-network.com/news/amazon-cuts-approximately-1000-roles)

item.title: RBI clarifies FEMA rules, exempts personal transactions and tutoring payments
item.description:
RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra yesterday clarified that individuals undertaking personal‑nature transactions, overseas tutoring payments, and small software assignments are exempt from reporting under the new FEMA rules that took effect on October 1. The framework lets exporters file a self‑declaration for each export bill up to ₹10 lakh, with banks handling the reporting to the RBI.
Banks and authorised dealers will now receive the export declarations and match them with remittances, replacing the earlier SOFTEX process for software exports and the separate goods‑export declaration. The regulations introduce a single Export Declaration Form (EDF) that can cover a month’s worth of service exports, including software, allowing exporters to file one form instead of multiple. For each bill not exceeding ₹10 lakh, exporters may submit a self‑declaration to their authorised dealer, which the bank can then close in the export‑monitoring system once payment is realised. Exporters also have the option to file these self‑declarations quarterly, enabling bulk closure of eligible entries in the export‑monitoring system. The RBI said it will publish FAQs to help freelancers, creators and SaaS founders understand how the clarification applies to their specific arrangements, especially regarding overseas tutoring and small software assignments.
“From a founder's perspective, there's not a whole lot of change... what was being filed in SOFTEX, they'll go by and file it in EDF and the banks have to match,” Naganand Doraswamy, founder and managing partner at Ideaspring Capital said.
“consolidating export reporting through authorised banks could simplify compliance for software and AI startups,” Manav Garg, cofounder and managing partner at Together Fund said.
